gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a built-in cable holds beyond its single-device peak: Smartzone measured the UGREEN 100W retractable charger falling from 100 W to 65 W after an average of 35 minutes at constant load, and no result puts each cable's peak watts, sustained or measured watts and watts with a second device plugged in side by side.
standout_why: Compared against UGREEN US's retractable page (read; names and prices only in the part read), Belkin's two support articles (read; 67 W single use and a 45 W + 20 W split, but cable and port are not separated), ChargerLAB's teardown (read; label lines of 20 V 5 A for the cable and PPS 5-21 V 5 A, no sustained-load or two-device figures) and Android Authority's Baseus CJ11 review (read; not in ChatGPT's results). Only Belkin's page gives a two-device split, for its own charger. None has the 35-minute drop to 65 W, and none normalises peak, sustained and shared watts across models. The Verge page ChatGPT cited could not be opened, and the UGREEN US product page ChatGPT cited returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so its multi-port table was not compared.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN Nexode 100W as the pick for most watts through the cable, but with a footnote: 100 W is a peak that Smartzone saw held for about 35 minutes before the charger settled at 65 W. On a long laptop session that puts it level with the roughly 65 W Android Authority measured through the Baseus CJ11 cable and near Belkin's 67 W single-use figure. With a second device plugged in the cables converge at about 45 W: Belkin states 45 W + 20 W, Android Authority measured 45 W to a MacBook on the Baseus, UGREEN's 65W gives its cable about 45 W with three devices, and ESR caps both outputs at 45 W combined. So the 100 W model wins for a single laptop filling from low; for laptop plus phone, cable length (ESR 3.1 ft, Belkin 3.3 ft retail) and price separate the rows more than headline watts. ChatGPT's first answer described the Baseus CJ11 as two retractable cables plus one port, while the unit Android Authority tested has one cable and two ports, so the page should name the variant.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X606)
findings.label: Sustained output at a constant 100 W load
findings.value: 100 W for an average of 35 minutes, then 65 W; 57 °C housing and 73 °C ports at that point
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 100W Ladegerät mit einziehbarem Kabel im Test (Smartzone, Jan, 21 August 2025)
findings.note: Smartzone used an electronic load on a German-market unit; the article does not say whether the load was on the built-in cable or on USB-C1. Both share the same 20 V 5 A profile. Read through a machine translation of the German page.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X606)
findings.label: Built-in cable rating printed on the label, and protocols measured on the cable
findings.value: 5V3A, 9V3A, 12V3A, 15V3A, 20V5A, 100W Max; PPS 5-21 V at up to 5 A; no AVS listed
findings.source_title: Teardown of the UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable - ChargerLAB
findings.note: ChargerLAB read protocols with a POWER-Z KM003C. USB-C1 has the same profile; USB-C2 is 30 W max and USB-A 22.5 W max. The teardown lists no AVS on any output, so by the cluster rule this 100 W cable does not give an iPhone 18 Pro its top tier.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X606)
findings.label: Cable length, measured
findings.value: about 72.5 cm (28.5 in, 2.38 ft) per ChargerLAB; 70 cm per Smartzone
findings.source_title: Teardown of the UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable - ChargerLAB
findings.note: 72.5 cm ÷ 30.48 = 2.38 ft, a little under the 2.5 ft in our record. Smartzone's 70 cm is from https://www.smartzone.de/ugreen-nexode-100w-ladegeraet-mit-einziehbarem-kabel-im-test/ read the same day.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W Charger with Retractable USB-C Cable (X606)
findings.label: Multi-port behaviour
findings.value: Static, not dynamic, distribution; USB-C2 and USB-A drop to 7.5 W each when used together; with two ports in parallel PPS narrows to 5-11 V at 4.5 A on the first port
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 100W Ladegerät mit einziehbarem Kabel im Test (Smartzone)
findings.note: Smartzone's full split tables are images and could not be read, so the cable's exact share with a second device is in 'unsourced'. 11 V × 4.5 A = 49.5 W is the PPS ceiling in two-port use (my arithmetic).

findings.product: Belkin UltraCharge Retractable GaN Wall Charger 67W

findings.label: Measured watts through the built-in cable against the ports
findings.value: Built-in cable roughly 65 W to a MacBook Air M3; 69.14 W from the USB-C ports; Pixel 10 Pro XL 34.5 W on the cable against 37.45 W and 36.62 W on the ports

findings.note: Rita El Khoury attributes the Pixel's lower cable reading to the battery already filling. The reviewed unit has one retractable cable and two USB-C ports.

findings.label: Two devices, cable length, list price
findings.value: MacBook 45 W while the Pixel 10 Pro XL dropped from 18 V to 9 V and took about 20-23 W; 32 in (about 82 cm, 2.7 ft) cable; MSRP $59.99
findings.source_title: Baseus EnerCore CJ11 USB-C wall charger review (Android Authority, Rita El Khoury)
findings.note: The review does not say which output fed the MacBook in the two-device test, gives no reel cycle figure and does not mention AVS. $59.99 is the MSRP the review states, not a price read at a store today.

findings.product: Anker Nano Charger 35W with Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable (A2658)
findings.label: Cable output, two-port total, length, reel rating, price
findings.value: 35 W max from the cable or the port alone (20 V 1.75 A); two ports in use 35 W max total; 2.3 ft cable; 20,000 bends and 20,000 retractions; $19.99 (was $29.99), in stock
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charger (35W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: Anker marks the reel figures as internal testing. The US page gives no per-port split for two devices.

findings.label: Output per ESR's support page
findings.value: 5-20 V at up to 3 A; 45 W maximum total when both outputs are in use; PPS and AVS listed
findings.source_title: ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger - ESR help page (2D001)
findings.note: 20 V × 3 A = 60 W is the electrical ceiling of the stated range (my arithmetic). This page gives no voltage ranges for PPS or AVS, no fixed two-device split and no 60 W statement.

findings.label: Rated watts against the 60 W peak, and cable length
findings.value: Rated 45 W; 'ESR says the output can peak at up to 60W when a single device asks for more'; 3.1 ft built-in cable
findings.source_title: ESR's New Charger Means Never Packing a Charging Cable Again (Techlicious, Palash Volvoikar, 6 September 2026)
findings.note: Palash Volvoikar adds that ESR 'hasn't really detailed how often you'll see that peak figure', so 60 W is a maker's peak claim, not a measurement. The article's $35.99 launch price is not today's price.

findings.label: Reel ratings count different things
findings.value: Anker: 20,000 retractions + 20,000 bends; UGREEN 65W: 25,000 retractions + 10,000 bends; Belkin: no number; Android Authority and Techlicious give none for Baseus or ESR
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Charger (35W, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) - Anker US
findings.note: All are makers' own claims; no independent reel test was found. UGREEN's figure is via Cubed3 (https://www.cubed3.com/tech/reviews/accessories/ugreen-nexode-65-w-gan-fast-charger-with-retractable-cable), Belkin's absence via https://www.belkin.com/support-article/?articleNum=337690.
